country: Burundi; Kenya; Rwanda; Tanzania, United Republic of; Uganda
geo_scope: It affected locations in more than one state, province, or region
gov_just_details: The Communications Authority of Kenya (CA) said on Jun. 24 they had "no intention whatsoever to shutdown Internet traffic or interfere with the quality of connectivity". Through statements from ISP officials, which were a mix of denials and contradictions (linked in telco_ack_quote), the government used an excuse of a subsea cable cut to deny the shutdown. However, independent reports and anonymous sources confirmed that the internet was deliberately cutoff through orders by the Kenyan government to disconnect circuits at sea cable landing stations.
telcos_involved: Kenya: Airtel (Bharti Airtel), Kenya: Faiba (Jamii Telecom), Kenya: Safaricom, Kenya: Wananchi
telco_ack_quote: Safaricom sent a customer notice claiming the disruptions to both internet services and the M-PESA electronic payment app are a result of “an outage on two of our under sea cables.” Airtel issued a similar notice, indicating disruptions to undersea cables have impacted their services.
event: The internet was shutdown in Kenya from 13:30 to 20:45 (UTC+0) on Jun. 25 as evident by severe disruptions from multiple measurement sources. Authorities went back on their word not to shutdown the internet, and ISPs denied or contradicted themselves after the shutdown had occurred. According to indepedent and anonymous sources, Kenyan authorities ordered the tampering of subsea cable landing stations in order to shutdown the internet, which gave the appearance of a cable cut which are common in the region. Since they couldn't differentiate between inland circuits, four other countries had severe internet disruptions at the same time as well: Burundi, Rwanda, Tanzania, and Uganda. The shutdown coincided with a violent crackdown on protestors, including the firing of live rounds and tear gas, which resulted in at least five deaths and dozens of injuries on Jun. 25 alone.

The rationale behind the decision was an attempt to curb online crimes and call centers operating in the area. Parts of Myanmar in Tachileik township, and western Laos including Kings Romans Casino, experienced the shutdown.

actual_cause_details: There was a partial internet shutdown in Cameroon as votes were still being counted from a recent election and widespread protests were underway
event: There was a partial shutdown across Cameroon between 3:30am and 8:30pm (UTC+0) on Oct. 23 in the midst of ongoing vote counting and widespread protests. CamTel and MTN blamed the outage on a problem with the landing station of the WACS submarine cable. Neighboring Central African Republic (CAR) also experienced a disruption between 3:30am and 6:30pm (UTC+0) on the same day, and both countries had connectivity return relatively quickly, supporting the notion that the Cameroon branch of the WACS cable was tampered with given the CAR's downstream reliance on internet coming through sub cables via Cameroon. This was the first shutdown experienced in CAR.
